problem_statement:
guangzhengli/nextjs-blog-template is a runnable Next.js 15 App Router blog (content-collections MDX posts, a shared header with a mobile sheet menu, a table of contents and a comments shell), here dressed as Kettle & Coil, a home coffee-roasting field journal by Delia Marchetti. The home feed (/) shows an intro and a 'Featured roast logs' section; /blog/ is the full roast-log index and /blog/intro/, /blog/hello-world/ and the other roast logs are articles, all sharing the Kettle & Coil header and theme. Six roast logs are tagged by category (Technique, Sourcing, Equipment).

The site's own browse control is a 'Browse the roast log' finder: a row of category tabs (All / Technique / Sourcing / Equipment) sits above the roast-log cards and drives which cards are shown, with a live readout that reports the count (e.g. 'Showing 6 of 6 · All logs', and after picking Sourcing, 'Showing 2 of 6 · Sourcing'). The finder appears on BOTH the home feed (above the featured logs) and the full roast-log index at /blog/, so a reader can filter from either surface. It is a React client component (src/components/roast-filter.tsx) that filters a serialisable post list and renders the tab row, the readout and the responsive card grid; its layout lives in src/components/roast-filter.css.

Three regressions were reported against the finder and must all be repaired so the reference behaves correctly:
(1) MOBILE OVERFLOW — on a 390px phone the home page scrolls sideways. The finder's tab row is laid out as a FIXED-WIDTH, NON-WRAPPING flex line (.roast-filter__tabs is `display:flex; flex-wrap:nowrap; width:760px` with each .roast-filter__tab pinned to `min-width:150px`), so the row can never shrink below ~760px and pushes the document past the right edge of a 390px viewport (the tablet and desktop viewports are wide enough to contain it). Fix: let the tab row wrap and let the tabs shrink so the home page fits the phone with no horizontal scroll.
(2) BROKEN CARD GRID — on the default desktop finder view the card grid is forced to a fixed three-track template far wider than its container and the cards carry cascading negative margins with z-stacking, so the cards shingle and collide into an overlapping, clipped pile and the active tab renders as near-white text on a near-white pill (illegible). Fix: use a responsive auto-fit grid with no negative-margin overlap and a legible active-tab treatment, so every card and tab is readable.
(3) STALE COUNT — clicking a category tab must actually filter the cards and update the readout. In the broken build the shown cards and the readout are seeded once at mount and never recomputed, so clicking Sourcing highlights the tab but the grid keeps all six cards and the readout stays frozen at 'Showing 6 of 6 · All logs'. Fix: recompute the shown cards and the readout from the active category on every tab change.

Repair the roast-log finder so: the home page has no horizontal scroll on a 390px phone (the tab row wraps and the tabs shrink); the desktop finder shows a clean, legible card grid with no shingled/overlapping cards; clicking a category tab filters the cards and updates the readout to 'Showing N of 6 · <Category>'; and the finder is present on both the home feed and the /blog/ index. Preserve the Kettle & Coil content, the six roast logs and their categories, the featured feed, the section order and the visual system, and keep the desktop and tablet reading layouts coherent.

(Note: this project is served as a Next.js static export over a static file server; the offline build infrastructure -- switching next.config.ts to `output:'export'` with `trailingSlash:true` and unoptimized images plus `dynamic='force-static'` on the sitemap/robots routes, dropping the remote lxgw-wenkai webfont <link> from app/layout.tsx, stubbing the remote Giscus comments widget to render nothing, relaxing the body from `overflow-x-hidden` to `min-w-0` so overflow is observable, and rebranding the demo copy from the generic 'Nextjs Blog Template' into Kettle & Coil -- is supplied identically in all evaluation legs and is not part of the repair work.)
required_content: Repair the roast-log finder so the home page has no horizontal scroll on a 390px phone: the category tab row (.roast-filter__tabs) wraps and the tabs shrink instead of sitting in a fixed 760px non-wrapping row.

Repair the finder's desktop card grid so it is a clean, legible responsive grid: no shingled or overlapping cards (no cascading negative margins), and a legible active-tab treatment (not near-white text on a near-white pill).

Wire the category filter so clicking a tab (Technique / Sourcing / Equipment / All) filters the shown roast-log cards AND updates the live readout to 'Showing N of 6 · <Category>' (e.g. 'Showing 2 of 6 · Sourcing'); the readout and grid must not stay frozen at the initial 'Showing 6 of 6 · All logs'.
Render the roast-log finder on BOTH the home feed and the full roast-log index at /blog/, so both routes carry the category browse control.
Preserve the Kettle & Coil content, the six roast logs and their categories, the 'Featured roast logs' feed, and the visual system; keep the desktop and tablet reading layouts coherent.
Introduce no new console or network errors in any captured state.
design_constraints: Keep the 'Browse the roast log' finder above the 'Featured roast logs' feed on the home page and at the top of the /blog/ roast-log index, with its four category tabs and the live count readout.

The tab row must wrap and the tabs must shrink on a phone (no fixed 760px non-wrapping row); the card grid must be a responsive grid that collapses cleanly to one column on mobile with no overlapping cards.
Clicking a category tab must recompute both the shown cards and the readout string from the active category (no stale snapshot seeded once at mount).
Preserve the Kettle & Coil content and the home / index structure and visual system (intro, social links, featured feed, roast-log cards, card rhythm, border radius, muted-surface treatment).
Do not introduce any console pageerrors or failed network requests in any captured state.
state_constraints: desktop_home verifies the home feed renders the roast-log finder above the featured feed within the 1440px viewport with no horizontal overflow.
mobile_home verifies the finder's tab row wraps so the home page has no horizontal overflow on a 390px phone (a primary discriminator).
mobile_filter_component verifies the finder scrolled into view has no horizontal overflow on a 390px phone.
tablet_home verifies the 834px tablet viewport contains the home layout with no horizontal overflow.
desktop_filter_component verifies the finder's default (All) view renders a clean, legible card grid with no shingled/overlapping cards (the visual-regression anchor).

desktop_sourcing_filter verifies that clicking the Sourcing tab filters the cards and updates the readout to 'Showing 2 of 6 · Sourcing' (the interaction discriminator), changed from the pre-click 'Showing 6 of 6 · All logs'.
desktop_blog verifies the /blog/ roast-log index carries the same finder (a cross-route presence discriminator).
mobile_blog verifies the /blog/ index carries the finder and has no horizontal overflow on a 390px phone.
desktop_post verifies an article route (/blog/intro/) still renders the shared Kettle & Coil header and theme after the change.

change_completion: The home page renders within the viewport on a 390px phone with no horizontal scroll (the finder tab row wraps and the tabs shrink).
Clicking a category tab filters the roast-log cards and updates the readout to 'Showing N of 6 · <Category>' instead of staying frozen at 'Showing 6 of 6 · All logs'.
The roast-log finder renders on both the home feed and the /blog/ roast-log index with its four category tabs and readout.
design_consistency: Reuses the home / index shell, the featured feed and the Kettle & Coil theme and card treatment.
The finder's card grid is a clean, legible responsive grid with no overlapping cards and a legible active-tab pill.
regression: The home content (intro, social links, finder, featured roast logs) remains intact.
The desktop and tablet reading layouts remain coherent and the article route still renders the shared header.
No console pageerrors or failed network requests are introduced in any captured state.
responsive: Mobile renders the home page and the /blog/ index within the viewport with no horizontal scroll.
Tablet and desktop layouts remain coherent; the finder card grid collapses cleanly to one column on a phone.

author_notes:
Native-lever L4 (editorial_blog, Next.js 15 App Router static export). The lever is the blog's OWN browse control: a 'Browse the roast log' category filter (React client component src/components/roast-filter.tsx) with tabs All / Technique / Sourcing / Equipment over the six roast-log post cards and a live readout 'Showing N of 6 · <Category>'. It renders on the home feed and the /blog/ roast-log index. Four orthogonal gates discriminate the legs:
D6 no_horizontal_overflow: the finder's .roast-filter__tabs row is a fixed non-wrapping flex line (`display:flex; flex-wrap:nowrap; width:760px`, each .roast-filter__tab `min-width:150px`) that cannot shrink below ~760px and overflows a 390px phone (baseline+bad measure ~1239px on mobile_home vs 0 for the reference wrap layout `flex-wrap:wrap` / `flex:0 1 auto`). Desktop/tablet are wide enough that the tab row alone fits; the mobile states are the D6 discriminators.
D3 visual_regression (desktop_filter_component + mobile_filter_component): the broken finder forces the card grid to a fixed three-track `repeat(3,520px)` template with cascading negative margins (`margin-left:-360/-300/-420/-320/-380px`) and z-stacking, so the six cards shingle and collide into an overlapping, clipped pile, and the active tab is near-white text (#f7f5f2) on a near-white pill (#f3f0ec) — illegible. This is a real geometry break over the whole lever region (tab row AND card grid), not a recolor; the reference is a clean auto-fit `minmax(230px,1fr)` grid with a legible dark active pill.
D2 dom_assertions (cross-route): the finder is rendered from a per-surface whitelist. The reference whitelists both 'home' and 'blog', so the finder title/tabs are present on desktop_blog and mobile_blog; the baseline and bad whitelist 'home' only, so the /blog/ index route has no finder — they fail the .roast-filter__title / .roast-filter__tab assertions on desktop_blog and mobile_blog. The home page carries the finder in all legs, so D3/D4/D6 (measured on home) stay orthogonal to the D2 route axis.
D4 interaction_assertions (desktop_sourcing_filter, changed_from desktop_filter_component): clicking the Sourcing tab must set the readout to 'Showing 2 of 6 · Sourcing'. The reference recomputes shown cards + readout from the active category on every click. The bad build tracks the active tab in one state but seeds the shown list and the readout from a lazy `useState(() => posts)` / `useState(() => 'Showing 6 of 6 · All logs')` initializer that is never recomputed, so the click flips the active-tab highlight (interaction registers, status succeeded) but the grid keeps all six cards and the readout stays frozen — D4 fails on the terminal state. The baseline keeps the CORRECT filter wiring (only its CSS is broken) so it PASSES D4 — strict-subset failure: baseline fails D6+D3+D2 and passes D4, bad fails all four.
Leg-varying files: src/components/roast-filter.tsx (reference/baseline = correct wiring; bad = frozen snapshot), src/components/roast-filter.css (reference = responsive; baseline/bad = broken grid+tabs), src/lib/roast-filter-surfaces.ts (reference = home+blog; baseline/bad = home-only). The infrastructure (output:'export' build, dropped webfont link, stubbed Giscus, relaxed body overflow, six categorised roast logs, the roast-filter host wiring in src/app/page.tsx and src/app/blog/page.tsx, and the Nextjs Blog Template -> Kettle & Coil rebrand) is supplied identically in all three legs. Tailwind is the styling system; the finder adds a small scoped stylesheet. Assets: /kettle-coil-mark.svg on the home intro.
